canDo: Can organise scattered events into a linear story and accurately report what others said or asked.
review: Review past tenses and relative pronouns; learn present-tense reported speech: dire/expliquer que, demander si/question words.
input: Read two short stories and extract their structure.
output: Write 150 words about an experience; speak for 3 minutes, adding detail with relative pronouns.
checkpoint: Can turn at least 6 direct statements/questions into reported speech while keeping the story’s timeline clear.
challenge: Today’s challenge: listen to a news item on RFI’s Journal en français facile and report it in 4 sentences (Le journaliste explique que… / Il ajoute que… / Un témoin raconte que…), add 1 relative clause (qui / que / où) for detail, then read it aloud to yourself.

questions.why: « Qu'est-ce que vous entendez, en ce moment ? » — the rapids on the right correspond to only one of the three areas.
They kept looking for the same specific piece of information, and found it faster in the old shared file.
« sans elle, nous n'aurions pas su quelles questions poser », but those questions could have been asked earlier.
An administrative reason: exit formalities had been completed, so they couldn’t leave the ship.
Scheduled for 21:00, it actually left at 9 h 20 the next day — about twelve hours twenty minutes.
« ce que la commune aurait refusé » — they applied instead for insulation work eligible for a regional grant.
The backups had been failing since Friday, and the disk only died on Tuesday; Marc leaving affected the email address, not when the backups started failing.
« C'est là que j'ai rencontré les gens » happened after she was forced to stay.
« tant que j'avais une porte de sortie chaque week-end, je la prenais », and she says plainly there’s no need to wait for a cancelled train.
She lost her regulars within three months, while new customers didn’t yet know she existed.
« conduite hésitante » left both him and his instructor unsure what to change.
Checking the mirrors three times — not too little, but too much.
